sourcedFrom: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. (2025)
cleanIntro: A 9mm pistol built on 1911 lines, the longer bushing-barrel sibling of the EDC X9 2.0: a thumb safety on the left of the frame, a bushing barrel with the recoil spring plug held under the barrel bushing, a guide rod carrying a Shok-Buff, a backstrap that swings away when the hammer spring housing is pressed in from the bottom of the frame, and grip panels held on by grip screws. Wilson Combat's schedule is round-counted: a quick clean every 300 rounds, a thorough clean and Shok-Buff check every 1,200, and the firing pin and trigger group every 6,000. ⛔ The recoil spring plug is under heavy spring tension when the bushing turns — keep it captured, glasses on, pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Magazine out before anything else
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine release on the left of the frame, take the magazine out of the grip and put it down away from the pistol.
steps.prose: Magazine first, slide second. Run the slide with a loaded magazine still in and you have just chambered a round.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Unloading, step 1, p.35

steps.title: Thumb safety down, then retract the slide
steps.action: Push the thumb safety at the left rear of the frame down to FIRE. Then pull the slide fully back to extract and eject anything in the chamber.
steps.prose: With the safety up on SAFE the slide is blocked and will not move — that is the safety working, not a jam. Do not force the slide against it.
steps.quote: The slide will not retract, and you will not be able to load the handgun if the safety is in the SAFE (up)(a) position.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Loading the Chamber and Activating the Safety, p.32

steps.title: Look and feel: chamber empty, magazine out
steps.action: With the slide held back, look into the chamber and the magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber. Both checks, every time.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat asks for the check to be visual and physical. A dark chamber can hide a cartridge from the eye; it cannot hide it from a finger.
steps.quote: Visually and physically confirm there is not a cartridge in the chamber, and the magazine is not in the handgun.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Unloading, step 3, p.35

steps.title: Eye protection on, bushing wrench and 1/8-inch punch to hand
steps.action: Put on safety glasses before you start, and have a non-marring bushing wrench and the takedown tool that came with the pistol, or a 1/8-inch steel punch, on the bench — the bushing step needs the wrench and the backstrap step needs the tool.
steps.prose: The recoil spring plug comes out under heavy spring tension in this strip, and a plug that gets away goes for your face. The pistol is proven empty before any of it starts.
steps.aside: Remove magazine, retract slide, and visually inspect chamber to ensure your pistol is unloaded.
steps.quote: Wear adequate eye protection when disassembling this or any firearm.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 1, p.51

steps.title: Slide forward, thumb safety on
steps.action: With the pistol proven empty, let the slide go forward on the empty chamber under control, then push the thumb safety up to SAFE. The slide stays locked in battery for the bushing work.
steps.prose: The safety holds the slide still while you turn the bushing. It comes off again before the slide stop is pushed out.
steps.quote: Lower slide and engage thumb safety.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 2 (the second step printed as 2), p.52

steps.title: Press the plug in, turn the bushing clockwise
steps.action: Fit the non-marring bushing wrench over the barrel bushing, press the recoil spring plug in with it, and slowly rotate the bushing clockwise, keeping the plug captured under the wrench as the bushing turns off it.
steps.prose: Slowly, and with the plug held: once the bushing clears it, the only thing holding a compressed recoil spring is your wrench.
steps.quote: Depress recoil spring plug with a non-marring bushing wrench and slowly rotate bushing clockwise while capturing the recoil spring plug.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 3, p.53

steps.title: Ease the plug out, slowly
steps.action: Let the recoil spring plug come forward out of the slide slowly, under control, until the spring is relaxed, then set the plug aside. Muzzle pointed in a safe direction throughout.
steps.prose: ⛔ Wilson Combat calls this assembly under heavy spring tension. Never point the muzzle end at yourself or anyone while the plug is coming out.
steps.quote: Slowly ease the plug out of the slide and set aside.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 4, p.54
steps.warn: This assembly is under heavy spring tension-always wear safety glasses and point in a safe direction.

steps.title: Safety off, half-moon notch aligned, slide stop out
steps.action: Push the thumb safety back down. Move the slide until the slide stop lines up with the rear takedown notch — the half-moon cut-out in the slide — then push the slide stop shaft through from right to left, take the slide stop off and set it aside.
steps.prose: The half-moon is the one to line up with. Pushed out against a misaligned slide, the slide stop drags across the frame.
steps.quote: Disengage thumb safety, align slide until the slide lock aligns with the rear takedown notch (half moon cut out on slide) and push the slide stop shaft from right to left and set aside.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 5, p.55

steps.title: Slide assembly off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide assembly forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: With the plug already out and the spring relaxed, the slide comes off without a fight. If it binds, the slide stop is not fully out.
steps.quote: At this time you can remove the slide assembly from the frame.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 6, p.56

steps.title: Recoil spring, bushing, then barrel out of the slide
steps.action: Take the recoil spring and its guide rod out of the slide, then the barrel bushing, then the barrel. If the bushing is a tight fit, tap it out lightly using the barrel.
steps.prose: Light taps only, with the barrel as the drift — not a hammer and not a steel punch on a fitted bushing.
steps.aside: If the bushing is a tight fit in the slide, use the barrel to tap the bushing out of the slide with light tapping.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring, barrel bushing, and barrel from the slide assembly.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 7, p.57

steps.title: Hammer down carefully onto its rest
steps.action: On the frame, lower the hammer under control so it rests against the front of the hammer slot. Do not let it fall freely.
steps.prose: ⛔ Wilson Combat warns that skipping this can damage the pistol: the backstrap that comes off next holds the hammer spring housing, and it is released with the hammer at rest.
steps.quote: Lower the hammer carefully, so it is at rest with the front of the hammer slot in the frame.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 8, p.58
steps.warn: Failure to do so can damage your firearm.

steps.title: Takedown tool in, backstrap swings away
steps.action: Put the takedown tool into the hole at the bottom of the frame and compress the hammer spring housing, while pressing upward on the bottom of the backstrap's beavertail. When the backstrap swings freely, pivot it away from the grip.
steps.prose: Both pressures at once — the tool compressing the housing and your thumb lifting the beavertail. With only one, the backstrap stays put.
steps.quote: Insert the included takedown tool in the hole at the bottom of the frame, compress the hammer spring housing at the same time, while placing upward pressure on the bottom of the backstrap beavertail.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 9, p.59

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is the strip as Wilson Combat writes it for the EDC X9L 2.0: slide, barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring and guide rod with the Shok-Buff, the recoil spring plug, the slide stop, and the backstrap swung away. The grip panels stay on — they are held by grip screws and are not part of this strip. Look every part over for abnormal wear or breakage now.
steps.prose: Any part showing damage, unusual wear or breakage means the pistol is not used until Wilson Combat has been contacted. The firing pin and the trigger group are a round-count job, in Deep Clean.
steps.aside: Inspect all parts for abnormal wear and breakage at this time.
steps.quote: You now have the frame disassembled as needed for normal cleaning and lubrication.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Fieldstripping the EDC X9L 2.0 Pistol: Disassembly, step 10, p.60

steps.title: The bore: slow, full-length strokes with a nylon brush
steps.action: Put a 9mm nylon bore brush on a cleaning rod, wet it with bore cleaner, and run it through the bore, pushing all the way through on every stroke. Let it stand 3 to 5 minutes, then wipe it clean with dry patches. Wipe the chamber, the barrel exterior and the barrel bushing too.
steps.prose: Full-length strokes, not short scrubbing — reversing a brush halfway down the bore is hard on the brush and the rod.
steps.aside: Allow to stand for 3 to 5 minutes then wipe clean with a dry patch.
steps.quote: When cleaning the bore, use slow complete strokes (full length of bore) with a properly sized nylon brush.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

steps.title: Wipe away dirt and fouling, inside and out
steps.action: Wipe the slide and frame rails, the breech face and the inside of the slide with non-abrasive patches or swabs. Where the inside of the pistol is caked with carbon, apply a carbon remover or bore cleaner first and let it work.
steps.prose: Non-abrasive is the word that matters on a finished pistol: nothing that scratches the rails or the finish.
steps.quote: Wipe away dirt and fouling on the interior and exterior of the firearm with non-abrasive patches or swabs.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

steps.title: Shok-Buff off the guide rod and inspected, every clean
steps.action: Take the Shok-Buff off the base of the guide rod, look at both sides, and replace it if it is cut, torn or swollen. Wipe the guide rod with a clean patch. Refit it with the groove at the top of the Shok-Buff aligned with the base of the guide rod, before the recoil spring goes back on.
steps.prose: ⚠ At the minimum the buffer is replaced every 1,200 rounds whatever it looks like.
steps.quote: At the minimum, replace the buffer every 1200 rounds.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Inspecting The Shok-Buff, p.67

steps.title: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces and the rails
steps.action: After cleaning, put a light film of oil on the moving parts — the barrel locking surfaces and lugs, the barrel hood, and the frame and slide rails. Light, not heavy.
steps.prose: Wilson Combat picks the oil by temperature: the regular oil at 60 degrees or warmer, the light oil below that.
steps.quote: Make sure to lubricate the barrel locking surfaces and frame/slide rails.
steps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — For Reliable Function, Clean And Lubricate, p.61

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Glasses on, rear of the slide pointed somewhere safe
deepSteps.action: Every 6,000 rounds Wilson Combat has the firing pin out to clean its channel and fit a new firing pin spring. Put on safety glasses and point the rear of the slide away from yourself and anyone else before you touch the firing pin stop.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The firing pin and its spring are under compression and can leave the slide hard — the book says it will shoot out as in a 1911.
deepSteps.quote: Before removing the firing pin and stop, make sure that the rear of the slide is pointed in a safe direction.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66
deepSteps.warn: Modern firearms contain springs that are under compression and can eject with significant striking force causing eye or other bodily injury.

deepSteps.title: Punch the firing pin in, stop down and out
deepSteps.action: Hold the rear of the slide firmly and press the firing pin in with a 1/8-inch punch to take the spring pressure off the stop. Keep a finger on the firing pin while you slide the stop down and out of the way, so the pin cannot eject.
deepSteps.prose: Your finger on the pin is what keeps it in the slide. Take it away before the stop is clear and the pin goes.
deepSteps.quote: Use your finger to retain the firing pin while sliding the stop down and out of the way.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66

deepSteps.title: Let the spring out slowly, then spring off the pin
deepSteps.action: Let the firing pin spring release its compression slowly, then take the pin and spring out of the slide. Separate them by turning the firing pin clockwise while pulling the spring firmly off. Clean the firing pin channel, and fit a new firing pin spring when it goes back in — the old one is discarded.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin spring is part of the drop safety: Wilson Combat has it changed every 5,000 rounds of live fire or 5,000 dry fires.
deepSteps.aside: Slowly allow the firing pin spring to release its compressed spring tension and then remove it from the slide.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin spring from the firing pin by turning the firing pin clockwise and firmly pulling off the spring.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Further Maintenance, Firing Pin Removal, p.66

deepSteps.title: Grip screws out, grip panels off
deepSteps.action: For the trigger group the grips come off. Thumb safety down to the firing position and the hammer lowered gently, then take out the grip screws with a screwdriver that fits them properly and lift the grip panels off the frame.
deepSteps.prose: A screwdriver that fits the slot is the point: a loose bit strips the screw heads or the threads in the frame bushings.
deepSteps.aside: Once the screws are removed, lift the grip panels off the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Use the appropriate screwdriver to carefully unscrew and remove the grip screws, taking care not to strip the screws or damage the threads.
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Replacing Grips & Backstrap, p.68

deepSteps.title: Trigger group: aerosol cleaner, then sparing oil
deepSteps.action: With the grip panels off, spray the trigger group components with an aerosol cleaner made for firearms, let it dry, and put a sparing amount of oil on the exposed parts of the trigger group.
deepSteps.prose: Sparingly is the instruction. The book directs cleaning these parts in place, not taking them out.
deepSteps.quote: Remove grips, clean trigger group components with aerosol cleaner designed for firearms use and re-lubricate exposed parts of trigger group sparingly
deepSteps.cite: Operation & Safety Manual for EDC X9 2.0 Handgun — Copyright© 2025 Wilson's Gun Shop, Inc. — Recommended Maintenance, Every 6000 rounds, p.64

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: 9mm nylon brush with bore cleaner, full-length strokes from end to end
Stand 3 to 5 minutes, then dry patches until clean
Chamber, barrel exterior and barrel bushing wiped

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and the inside of the slide wiped with non-abrasive patches
Carbon remover on anything caked, then wiped

cleaning.name: SHOK-BUFF
tasks: Off the guide rod, both sides inspected
Replaced if cut, torn or swollen — and every 1,200 rounds regardless
Refitted with its groove aligned to the base of the guide rod

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Light oil on the barrel locking surfaces, lugs and hood
Light oil on the frame and slide rails

reassembly: Backstrap pivoted back into place against the grip, over the hammer spring housing.
Barrel back into the slide, then the barrel bushing, then the recoil spring and guide rod with the Shok-Buff on the base of the rod, its groove aligned.
Slide assembly back onto the frame from the front, the half-moon takedown notch aligned with the slide stop, and the slide stop shaft pushed back in.
Thumb safety on, then the recoil spring plug pressed in with the bushing wrench and captured as the barrel bushing is turned back over it — glasses on, the plug is under heavy spring tension.
Wilson Combat's instruction is to reverse the disassembly steps; ease the slide forward on the empty pistol — never let it slam.
fncheck: Unloaded and proven, magazine out, muzzle in a safe direction — Wilson Combat asks for this test after every disassembly and reassembly. Thumb safety: cock the hammer, push the safety up to SAFE and press the trigger — the safety stays on and the hammer does not move. Disconnector: with the hammer cocked, draw the slide back ¼ to ½ inch and press the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Half-cock: set the hammer on half-cock and press the trigger with a full grip — the hammer must not move. If the hammer falls or moves in any of these, or you see it follow to half-cock when the slide closes, do not use the pistol and contact Wilson Combat.
